title: Sum over Subsets (SOS) DP & Submask Enumeration
relevance: Medium — rarely the first OA template, but “count / aggregate over all bit-subsets of a mask” and “partition a small set via submasks” show up in harder bit-mask screens; essential CF ~1700–2200 toolkit Striver never covers
company_notes: OA/interview appearances: puzzle/word letter-masks (enumerate submasks of a 7-letter puzzle); AND/OR compatibility (disjoint bits or covering flags); team/group partition for n ≤ 16 via O(3^n) DP; aggregate over bit-subsets at scale via CSES-style SOS on frequencies.

phases.goal: Candidate spots SOS vs submask-enumeration and the problem shapes that call for each.

must_hit.point: Recognize need, for every mask, of a sum/count/max over all its submasks (or supersets/complements) → SOS DP.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Says: when every mask needs an aggregate over i ⊆ mask (or supersets), use SOS.

must_hit.point: Recognize “split set mask into group sub + rest” / clique-partition / reconstruct-from-parts → submask enumeration transitions.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Names partition/split or clique-cover DP driven by walking sub ⊆ mask.

must_hit.point: Spot statement cues like compatible AND = 0, OR-subsets, count y with x|y=x or x&y=x.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Maps those phrasings to SOS or pairwise mask checks.

probes: When would you reach for SOS DP versus enumerating submasks of a fixed mask?
What problem wording suggests sum-over-subsets or complementary disjoint-pair SOS?

hints.1: Think about whether you need one aggregate per mask or must try every split of a set.
hints.2: Aggregates over all submasks/supersets → SOS; trying group sub + rest → (s-1)&m enumeration.
hints.3: n around 20 with per-mask submask aggregates → SOS; partition/clique cover needing each split → O(3^n) submask DP.

phases.goal: Candidate states the two tools and when each applies under typical bit-mask constraints.

must_hit.point: Submask enumeration: for fixed m, walk every s ⊆ m via for (s=m; s; s=(s-1)&m), handling 0 separately; over all masks this is O(3^n), not O(4^n).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Writes the (s-1)&m loop and cites O(3^n) for all (mask, submask) pairs.

must_hit.point: SOS: given A[0…2^n), compute F[mask]=Σ_{i⊆mask} A[i] (or sum over supersets) in O(n·2^n) by sweeping one bit at a time — an n-dimensional prefix sum on the subset lattice.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Describes bit-by-bit subset-lattice prefix sums yielding F as sum over submasks.

must_hit.point: Use submask enum when n ≤ 18ish for partition DP; switch to SOS when only aggregates are needed and n ≤ 20–23 makes n·2^n fit but 3^n/4^n does not.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Contrasts partition-DP n band with SOS when only aggregates matter at larger n.

probes: Walk through how you’d compute F[mask] = sum of A[i] over all i ⊆ mask efficiently.
Why is iterating all masks and all their submasks O(3^n) rather than O(4^n)?

hints.1: Each bit of the universe plays a fixed role in the (mask, submask) count.
hints.2: Per bit: off / in-mask-only / in-both → 3 choices → 3^n pairs.
hints.3: SOS adds along one bit dimension at a time: if bit i is on, F[mask] += F[mask^(1<<i)].

phases.goal: Candidate can write the submask loop, SOS / superset SOS, and the partition DP skeleton.

must_hit.point: Submask loop must be for (int s=m; s; s=(s-1)&m) plus explicit handling of s=0; never s-- alone.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Codes (s-1)&m and mentions adding the empty submask separately.

must_hit.point: SOS update: F=A; for i in 0..n-1: for mask: if mask>>i&1: F[mask] += F[mask^(1<<i)].
must_hit.evidence_hint: Gives the bit-on accumulation from the bit-cleared sibling.

must_hit.point: Sum over supersets: same loop but add into the bit-off side (F[mask^(1<<i)] += F[mask] when bit i is on), or SOS on bit-flipped indices.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Reverses the SOS flow into the unset-bit side or flips indices first.

must_hit.point: Partition template: dp[0]=0 (or 1 for ways); for mask: for sub=mask; sub; sub=(sub-1)&mask: dp[mask]=best(dp[mask], combine(score(sub), dp[mask^sub])).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Shows submask transitions combining score(sub) with dp on the complement bits.

probes: Write the SOS recurrence that fills F from A in one bit sweep.
How do you adapt the loop for sum-over-supersets or for partition DP?

hints.1: Start from copying A into F, then layer one bit dimension.
hints.2: When bit i is set, pull from (or push to) the mask with that bit cleared.
hints.3: Subset SOS: F[mask]+=F[mask^(1<<i)]; superset: F[mask^(1<<i)]+=F[mask]; partition: enumerate sub of mask and combine with mask^sub.

phases.goal: Candidate states the right bounds and which constraint band favors which tool.

must_hit.point: All (mask, submask) pairs cost 3^n because each bit is off / in-mask-only / in-both.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Explains the three-way per-bit accounting for 3^n.

must_hit.point: SOS (and inverse SOS with -= along each bit) runs in O(n·2^n).
must_hit.evidence_hint: States O(n·2^n) for the bit-dimension sweeps.

must_hit.point: Comfort band: n ≤ 20 / values ≤ 2^20 style constraints; n·2^n fits where 3^n/4^n may not when n ≤ 20–23.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Ties n·2^n feasibility to the n ≤ 20–23 / 2^20 setting versus heavier 3^n.

probes: What is the complexity of SOS versus enumerating every submask of every mask?
For which n would you prefer SOS aggregates over an O(3^n) partition DP?

hints.1: Count how many times each bit configuration appears in nested mask/submask loops.
hints.2: SOS is one pass per bit over the 2^n array; full submask enum hits 3^n pairs.
hints.3: Need splits → pay 3^n (n ≤ 18ish); only aggregates at n ≈ 20 → SOS O(n·2^n).

phases.goal: Candidate avoids wrong submask iteration and mis-applied SOS / disjoint-pair templates.

must_hit.point: Writing s-- (or otherwise decrementing without &m) visits non-submasks.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Warns that plain decrement leaves the subset lattice.

must_hit.point: Forgetting to handle s=0 separately after for (s=m; s; s=(s-1)&m) drops the empty submask.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Notes the loop condition skips 0 and must add it explicitly.

must_hit.point: Inverse SOS / Möbius: given F[mask]=Σ_{i⊆mask} A[i], recover A by subtracting along each bit (same loops, -=).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Describes undoing the prefix by -= on the same bit order.

must_hit.point: Compatible/disjoint pair template: store presence/value at each mask; SOS-max/OR into supersets; answer for x is SOS[((1<<B)-1)^x].
must_hit.evidence_hint: Queries the SOS of the bitwise complement of x after pushing onto supersets.

probes: What goes wrong if you iterate submasks with s-- instead of (s-1)&m?
How do you recover A from F after a sum-over-subsets transform?

hints.1: The loop body must stay inside bits of m.
hints.2: Empty mask is a valid submask; the nonzero loop misses it.
hints.3: Inverse uses the same bit sweeps with subtraction; disjoint queries look up SOS on the complement mask.

tradeoffs.topic: O(3^n) submask enumeration vs O(n·2^n) SOS
tradeoffs.strong_answer: Enumerate submasks when you must try splits of a set (partition / clique-cover / reconstruct-from-parts). Use SOS when you only need aggregates (sum/count/max) over all submasks or supersets of every mask — especially when n ≈ 20 makes n·2^n fit but 3^n/4^n does not.

tradeoffs.topic: Sum over subsets vs sum over supersets
tradeoffs.strong_answer: Subset SOS accumulates into bit-on masks from bit-cleared siblings. Superset SOS adds into the bit-off side when bit i is on, or runs ordinary SOS on bit-flipped indices — choose by whether queries need i ⊆ mask or supersets of mask.

gotchas.trap: Using s-- (or any decrement without &m) to walk submasks of m.
gotchas.correction: Use for (int s=m; s; s=(s-1)&m) so every step stays a submask of m; plain s-- visits non-submasks.

gotchas.trap: Omitting the empty submask after the nonzero (s-1)&m loop.
gotchas.correction: The loop stops before s=0; handle the empty submask separately whenever it is a valid case.

gotchas.trap: Paying O(3^n) partition-style enumeration when only per-mask aggregates are required.
gotchas.correction: If you need something for every mask from all its submasks and n≈20, switch to SOS O(n·2^n) instead of trying every split.

gotchas.trap: Leaving F as sum-over-subsets when the problem needs the original A (e.g. exact AND equals k after “AND ⊇ k” counts).
gotchas.correction: Apply inverse SOS / Möbius on the subset lattice: same bit loops with -= to recover A from F.
